native_result.query: In which years were individuals with a criminal record found to have significantly lower wealth compared to those without?
native_result.HypoA: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
native_result.HypoB: Across the three survey waves available in the NLSY79 incarceration subset, respondents with a criminal record (ever_jailed == 1) hold significantly less wealth than those without in every wave tested: 1985, 1990 and 1996. Mann-Whitney U (two-sided) with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across the three waves gives p_BH = 1.60e-10 (1985), 2.34e-34 (1990) and 1.39e-25 (1996); the rank-biserial correlation is r = -0.218, -0.420 and -0.351 respectively (all clearly above the |r| >= 0.05 practical threshold); and the median wealth of the ever_jailed=1 group (720 USD in 1985, 0 in 1990, 0 in 1996) is strictly below that of the ever_jailed=0 group (3,600; 10,500; 8,500 USD) in every wave. The gap widens over time in standardized (log-wealth) terms (Cohen's d from -0.23 in 1985 to -0.43 in 1996). All three declared conclusions hold; no year is exempt.
native_result.WorkflowB: Pipeline implemented in /workspace/artifacts/analysis.py and executed end-to-end. Steps: (1) load CSV, rename race typo 'hipanic' to 'hispanic' on 1,901 rows, document; (2) compute MIN_TOTAL = -866,400 over all three wealth columns and derive a single-comparable log1p(wealth - MIN_TOTAL + 1) per row per year; (3) for each year y in {1985, 1990, 1996}, run Mann-Whitney U (two-sided) on raw wealth and Welch t-test (two-sided) on log_wealth_y; (4) compute r rank-biserial from U and Cohen d on the log-transformed wealth using pooled SD; (5) apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR (alpha = 0.05) on the three Mann-Whitney p-values (primary) and on the three Welch p-values (sensitivity); (6) re-run Mann-Whitney after winsorizing at the 1st-99th percentile of wealth per year as sensitivity; (7) per year, declare significantly lower iff p_mw_BH < 0.05 AND median1 < median0 AND |r| >= 0.05; (8) ANNEX OLS with HC3 robust SE per year on log_wealth_y ~ ever_jailed * C(race) + ever_jailed * C(sex); (9) write results_summary.csv, sensitivity_winsor.csv, ols_annex.csv and README.md. Forbidden items (not executed per researcher constraints): no longitudinal, no permutations, no logit on wealth>0, no imputation.
